findings.title: Official fetch has socket timeout, no absolute wall deadline
findings.evidence: _open_official(..., timeout=30) ultimately passes urllib.open timeout, then response.read(2_000_001) may perform multiple blocking receives. The 600-second process-group supervision starts only after fetch and parsing. Thus a progressing/dripping response is not bounded to thirty seconds overall.
findings.required_outcome: Bound the complete official fetch to a real thirty-second wall deadline and retain fixed HTTPS endpoint, redirect refusal, byte bound and unmodified response evidence.

findings.title: Official scanner output is loaded before its byte bound is checked
findings.evidence: The subprocess writes scanner.json/scanner.stderr without output-size limits, then scanner.json.read_bytes() allocates the whole file before _json checks MAX_REPORT_BYTES. Its scanner timeout alone does not enforce memory/disk output bounds.
findings.required_outcome: Bound stdout/stderr growth or supervise their sizes, and bound reads before allocation while retaining failure evidence. Unknown/oversized/truncated output must fail, not be reinterpreted as complete coverage.
